channel.title: Kaiqian Zhang
channel.description: Notes on natural language processing, transformers, and machine learning.

item.title: A Day at the Agentic Biolab Workshop
item.description: What the frontier of AI for science actually looks like, from one day of talks at Princeton.

item.title: What the KV Cache Costs
item.description: The buffer that makes generation affordable is the reason serving a language model is hard.

item.title: The KV Cache
item.description: How a model avoids rereading the whole conversation every time it writes a word.

item.title: FFN-SwiGLU
item.description: The feed-forward layer holds most of a transformer's parameters, and the field demoted its activation to a gate that nobody can explain.

item.title: Pre-Norm vs. Post-Norm
item.description: Moving the normalizer off the main path is what made deep transformers trainable, and the argument over where to put it instead is still going.

item.title: RMSNorm vs. LayerNorm
item.description: Modern language models deleted one step from the operation that normalizes them, and the deleted step turns out to have been doing almost nothing.

item.title: RoPE
item.description: Position becomes an angle, the angle cancels, and what is left is a bank of clocks that the whole field is now busy retuning.

item.title: Attention
item.description: How a model lets each word look at the others, and why the formula divides by a square root.

item.title: My Mindmap of LLMs: Past Lives and Present
item.description: Every idea a transformer replaced was itself a fix for the thing before it, and the whole chain is one argument about how to represent a word.
